articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Traffic Congestion - Engineering the Solution' (Digest No.101)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Traffic Congestion - Engineering the Solution
IEE Colloquium on Traffic Congestion - Engineering the Solution
abstract: The author considers how a highway authority in the UK is using computer engineering to help relieve traffic congestion. The Royal County of Berkshire is used as the example. Different methods of using computer engineering to ease traffic congestion are discussed. The geographic information system; computer traffic modelling; urban traffic control systems and computer aided design of highways and bridges are looked at.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Combatting congestion: the role of road traffic informatics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Traffic Congestion - Engineering the Solution
abstract: The author highlights the case for the introduction of a more equitable form of paying for road-use, that of on-line variable road-use pricing. Options for this include a simple fixed toll, variable cordon-based charging and congestion-pricing. All options would require state-of-the-art road traffic informatics to realise a solution. Even then road-use pricing will offer only a part solution for our increasing traffic congestion problems, and must be considered as one measure within a carefully designed package of measures. The author describes some of the potential benefits of using new and emerging technologies to combat congestion and demonstrates that the technology is no longer a stumbling block to the introduction of road-use pricing. Finally, the author offers a brief insight into the system concepts and the technology developed by the PAMELA consortium within the EC's DRIVE programme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
